entities.summary: The Bakersfield sound is a sub-genre of country music developed in the mid-to-late 1950s in and around Bakersfield, California. Bakersfield is defined by its influences of rock and roll and honky-tonk style country, and its heavy use of electric instrumentation and backbeats. It was also a reaction against the slickly produced, orchestra-laden Nashville sound, which was becoming popular in the late 1950s. The Bakersfield sound became one of the most popular and influential country genres of the 1960s, initiating a revival of honky-tonk music and influencing later country rock and outlaw country musicians, as well as progressive country.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Bakersfield sound's influence on country music led to a revival of honky-tonk and shaped the development of outlaw country, with notable musicians such as Buck Owens and Merle Haggard emerging from this movement.
